SMTO-SKL-0179 — SMTO isn't sure if the GitHub release was published

GUID: ebc81e38-d2e8-5fd9-b397-151b2a6e9791
Slug: github-release-publish-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • SMTO asked GitHub to publish a draft release, but didn't get a clear answer back. The release may already be public, so publishing again could notify people twice or fail.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On github.com, open the GitHub project, select Releases, and find this release. Look for a Draft label next to it. If there's no Draft label, the release was published even though SMTO didn't get the confirmation.
  2. If it is already published, don't publish it again. Tell the Agent it is done. Publishing again isn't needed and could repeat announcements to people watching the project.
  3. Only if it still shows Draft, ask the Agent to publish it once more. A release that is still a draft was not published, so one new request is safe.

What success looks like

  • The release shows on the Releases page without a Draft label.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages releases for this project.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The release_publish request (draft=false) lost a reliable response and the follow-up read of the release could not confirm draft=false, so the publication may or may not have been applied.

What this means

  • Release publication raises mutation uncertainty after any supported desired-state readback cannot establish publication. The write may have applied despite its missing or invalid acknowledgement. Read exact provider state and reconcile it before another mutation; matching text alone does not prove attribution.

Why this can happen

  • Release publication raises mutation uncertainty after any supported desired-state readback cannot establish publication.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the exact release ID and inspect draft/publication state.

How to fix it

  • Do not publish again. Read the exact release ID with github.release or the Releases page and check its draft flag. draft=false shows the desired state but does not prove this request made the change; only if it is still a draft should a single new publish be requested.
